cards.text: These are the portions of Canaan the Israelites inherit, handed out by Eleazar the priest, Joshua son of Nun, Israel's leader, and the heads of the families of the tribes. The land for nine and a half tribes is assigned by lot, as the LORD commanded through Moses, Israel's leader before Joshua. Picture dividing up one cookie tray for a whole NATION, friend, with everybody leaning in to see who gets the corner piece.

cards.question: Only nine and a half tribes get land by lot here. Why not the other two and a half tribes?

answers.text: Moses already gave them land east of the Jordan
They will get the land left over at the end
They have to win their land in battle first

cards.text: The descendants of Joseph became two tribes, Manasseh and Ephraim. So Joseph basically showed up with a plus-one.

cards.question: One tribe gets no portion of the land: the Levites. But they still have flocks and herds. What are the Levites given instead?

answers.text: Cities to live in with pasturelands
Tents to camp in near the Jordan
Wells to water flocks in the wilderness

cards.text: So the Israelites divide the land, just as the LORD commanded Moses. Then the sons of Judah come to Joshua at Gilgal, and Caleb son of Jephunneh the Kenizzite walks up like someone who held onto his receipt: "You know what the LORD said to Moses the man of God at Kadesh-barnea about you and me."
Caleb was forty years old when Moses the servant of the LORD sent him from Kadesh-barnea to spy out the land, and he says he brought back an honest report.

cards.question: Caleb says his brothers who went with him made the hearts of the people melt with fear. What does Caleb say he did?

answers.text: He remained loyal to the LORD
He stayed quiet in the camp
He went back to spy again

cards.text: His brothers who went with him had the people's hearts melting like chocolate chips on a hot tray. But Caleb says that on that day, Moses swore him a promise about land.

cards.question: Moses swore that one stretch of land would be an inheritance for Caleb and his children forever. Which land?

answers.text: The land his feet had walked on

cards.text: Moses gave the reason: "…because you have wholly followed the LORD my God." Forty-five YEARS later, Caleb says the LORD has kept him alive, as He promised, while Israel wandered in the wilderness.

cards.question: Caleb was forty when Moses sent him to spy. Add those forty-five years. How old is Caleb now?
True or false: At eighty-five, Caleb says he's still as strong as he was the day Moses sent him out.

cards.text: Now Caleb asks for the hill country the LORD promised him that day, and he reminds Joshua that the Anakim were there, with great and fortified cities. Friend, they slid ME into a junk drawer when my edges went soft, and this man wants the HILL COUNTRY.

cards.question: The Anakim in that hill country have great and fortified cities. How does Caleb say he might drive them out?
True or false: Joshua turns Caleb down and gives that hill country to another tribe.

cards.text: Joshua blesses Caleb son of Jephunneh and gives him Hebron as his inheritance, and it still belonged to Caleb when this was written, because he wholly followed the LORD, the God of Israel. And get this: Hebron used to be called Kiriath-arba, after a man named Arba.

cards.question: Who was Arba, the man Kiriath-arba was named after?

answers.text: The greatest man among the Anakim

cards.text: Then the land had rest from war. You know that moment when the oven finally clicks off and the whole kitchen goes quiet? THAT.
